newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil weaker, slack buying pressures premium.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil weaker, slack buying pressures premium.

text.p: NWE spot gas oil prices were weaker on Friday with IPE gas oil easing in correction to Thursday's gains and slack buying interest putting barge and cargo premiums under pressure, traders said.

They said relaxed buying interest and good supply from Ventspils started to pressure premiums for 0.2 sulphur cargoes. Despite some light buying into Northern Germany this week a small backwardation between prompt and early August deliveries was wiped out and the market could tip further into contango.
In contrast diesel remained well supported with recent busy trade taking out most of the surplus.

But the market to the end of August looked fairly flat with premiums to the August screen contained in a +$4/+$5 range for deliveries by August 15 and Aug 16-31 deliveries around Sep IPE +$4.50/+$5 a tonne.
Brokers said the strong dollar versus the mark has pegged buyers firmly to the sidelines, helping to balance tight prompt ARA supply.
"Despite the tightish prompt (barge) supply only sellers are left for July ", one barge broker said.
Prompt and early August lifting barges were assessed flat with buying notionally around Aug evens to +25 cents.
Sellers were at 50 cents to +$1 fob ARA. Storage material was valued 50 cents to $1 under refinery oil.
Diesel barge premiums eased 50 cents to Aug +$4/$5 fob ARA.
